concepts.title: Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility
concepts.definition: As a consumer consumes more units of a commodity, the marginal utility derived from each successive unit goes on decreasing.
concepts.key_idea: Each additional unit gives less extra satisfaction than the previous one.
question_patterns: verify that marginal utility diminishes across units
find the unit at which MU becomes zero or negative
interpret a utility schedule using the law of diminishing MU
compute total utility when MU diminishes
identify saturation point from MU data

solution_steps.action: Compute marginal utilities for all units
solution_steps.explain: Use MU_n = TU_n - TU_(n-1).
Verify MU_n > MU_(n+1) for each successive unit.
The saturation point is the unit where MU becomes zero.

worked_examples.question: TU for units 1-5 is 10, 18, 24, 28, 30. Verify the law of diminishing MU and find the saturation point.
worked_examples.solution: MU = 10, 8, 6, 4, 2. MU decreases each unit. Saturation not yet reached since MU > 0 for all units (MU would be 0 at unit 6 if pattern continues).
worked_examples.answer: Law holds; saturation point beyond unit 5

worked_examples.question: MU for 6 units is 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 0. Find the saturation point.
worked_examples.solution: MU decreases from 12 to 0. MU = 0 at unit 6, so saturation is at unit 6.

exercises.question: TU for units 1-6 is 20, 38, 54, 68, 80, 90. Verify diminishing MU and find saturation point.
Explain why MU becomes negative beyond the saturation point.

concepts.title: Consumer Equilibrium - Single Commodity (Utility Analysis)
concepts.definition: A consumer is in equilibrium when marginal utility of a commodity in money terms equals its price. If MU_m > P, the consumer buys more; if MU_m < P, the consumer buys less.
concepts.formula: MU_x / P_x = MU_m, i.e. MU in money terms = Price
concepts.key_idea: Equilibrium occurs where marginal utility per rupee spent equals marginal utility of money.
question_patterns: find equilibrium quantity given MU schedule and price
verify consumer equilibrium for a single commodity
determine if consumer should buy more or less given MU and price
compute marginal utility in money terms
find price at which consumer is in equilibrium

solution_steps.explain: Divide marginal utility of each unit by marginal utility of money to get MU in money terms.

solution_steps.action: Compare MU in money terms with price
solution_steps.explain: Find the unit where MU in money terms equals price. If MU_money > P, buy more; if less, buy less.
The equilibrium quantity is the last unit for which MU in money terms is at least the price.

worked_examples.question: MU of good X for units 1-4 is 20, 18, 16, 14. Price is Rs 8 and MU of money is 2 utils. Find equilibrium quantity.
worked_examples.solution: MU in money terms: 10, 9, 8, 7. At unit 3, MU_money = 8 = price. At unit 4, MU_money = 7 < 8. So equilibrium at 3 units.

worked_examples.question: MU for units 1-3 is 50, 40, 30. Price = Rs 10, MU of money = 5. Find equilibrium.
worked_examples.solution: MU in money terms: 10, 8, 6. At unit 1, MU_money = 10 = price. Equilibrium at 1 unit.

exercises.question: MU for units 1-5 is 24, 20, 16, 12, 8. Price = Rs 4, MU of money = 4. Find equilibrium quantity.
Given MU schedule and price, determine whether the consumer should increase or decrease consumption at a given quantity.

concepts.title: Consumer Equilibrium - Two Commodities (Utility Analysis)
concepts.definition: A consumer spending income on two goods is in equilibrium when the ratio of marginal utility to price is equal for both goods and income is fully spent.
concepts.formula: MU_x / P_x = MU_y / P_y, subject to P_x*Q_x + P_y*Q_y = M
concepts.key_idea: Equilibrium requires equal marginal utility per rupee across both goods and full use of income.
question_patterns: find equilibrium combination of two goods given MU schedules and prices
verify whether a given combination is equilibrium
determine which good to consume more of given MU/P ratios
compute MU per rupee for two goods
allocate income between two goods to reach equilibrium

solution_steps.action: Compute MU per rupee for each unit of both goods
solution_steps.explain: Calculate MU_x/P_x and MU_y/P_y for each unit.

solution_steps.action: Allocate spending to equalize MU per rupee
solution_steps.explain: Spend on the good with higher MU per rupee until MU per rupee is equal across goods and income is exhausted.
Check that P_x*Q_x + P_y*Q_y = M and MU_x/P_x = MU_y/P_y.

worked_examples.question: MU_x for units 1-3 is 20, 18, 16; MU_y for units 1-3 is 24, 20, 16. P_x = 4, P_y = 4, income = 16. Find equilibrium.
worked_examples.solution: MU_x/P_x: 5, 4.5, 4. MU_y/P_y: 6, 5, 4. Buy 1 unit Y (6), 1 unit X (5), 1 unit Y (5), 1 unit X (4.5)... Spend: 1Y(4)+1X(4)+1Y(4)+1X(4)=16. At equilibrium: 2X, 2Y. MU_x/P_x = 4.5, MU_y/P_y = 5. Need equal. Re-allocate: 2X (4.5), 2Y (5). Better: 1X(5), 2Y(5) -> 4+8=12, not full. Try 2X, 2Y = 16. MU/P: 4.5 vs 5. Closest equal allocation within budget is 2X and 2Y.
worked_examples.answer: 2 units of X and 2 units of Y

worked_examples.question: MU_x: 40, 30, 20; MU_y: 30, 20, 10. P_x = 10, P_y = 5, income = 20. Find equilibrium.
worked_examples.answer: 1 unit of X and 2 units of Y

exercises.question: MU_x: 50, 40, 30; MU_y: 40, 30, 20. P_x = 10, P_y = 5, income = 25. Find equilibrium combination.
Verify whether buying 2 units of X and 1 unit of Y is equilibrium when MU_x/P_x = 3 and MU_y/P_y = 4 at that combination.

concepts.title: Indifference Curve Analysis
concepts.definition: An indifference curve is a curve showing different combinations of two goods that give the consumer the same level of satisfaction. Higher indifference curves represent higher satisfaction.
concepts.formula: MRS_xy = MU_x / MU_y (slope of indifference curve)
concepts.key_idea: All points on an indifference curve provide equal utility; the curve is convex to the origin due to diminishing MRS.
question_patterns: verify that two combinations lie on the same indifference curve
compute marginal rate of substitution between two goods
determine which indifference curve gives higher satisfaction
explain why indifference curves are convex to the origin
interpret properties of indifference curves

solution_steps.action: Identify the two combinations of goods
solution_steps.explain: Note the quantities of good X and good Y in each combination.

solution_steps.action: Check equal total utility or compute MRS
solution_steps.explain: Combinations on the same indifference curve yield equal total utility. MRS = |delta Y / delta X| = MU_x / MU_y.
If utilities are equal, the combinations lie on the same indifference curve. Higher utility means a higher curve.

worked_examples.question: Combination A gives (4X, 4Y) with utility 40; combination B gives (6X, 2Y) with utility 40. Are they on the same indifference curve?
worked_examples.solution: Both combinations give total utility of 40, so they lie on the same indifference curve.

worked_examples.question: At a point on an indifference curve, the consumer gives up 2 units of Y to gain 1 unit of X. Find MRS.
worked_examples.solution: MRS = |delta Y / delta X| = 2/1 = 2.

exercises.question: Explain why two indifference curves cannot intersect.
Combination A (3X, 5Y) gives utility 30; combination B (5X, 3Y) gives utility 30. Do they lie on the same indifference curve?

concepts.title: Budget Line and Budget Set
concepts.definition: The budget line shows all combinations of two goods that a consumer can afford given prices and income. The budget set is all combinations on or below the budget line.
concepts.key_idea: The budget line is a straight line whose slope is -P_x/P_y; it shifts with changes in income or prices.
question_patterns: find the equation of the budget line given prices and income
compute intercepts of the budget line on both axes
find combinations affordable within a budget
determine the effect of income change on the budget line
compute slope of the budget line

solution_steps.explain: Use P_x * X + P_y * Y = M.
X-intercept = M / P_x (all income on X); Y-intercept = M / P_y (all income on Y).

solution_steps.action: Compute slope and verify a combination
solution_steps.explain: Slope = -P_x / P_y. Check if a given combination satisfies P_x*X + P_y*Y <= M.

worked_examples.question: Income = Rs 100, P_x = Rs 5, P_y = Rs 10. Find the budget line equation and its intercepts.
worked_examples.solution: 5X + 10Y = 100. X-intercept = 100/5 = 20. Y-intercept = 100/10 = 10.

worked_examples.question: Income = Rs 60, P_x = Rs 4, P_y = Rs 6. Is the combination (8X, 4Y) affordable?

exercises.question: Income = Rs 120, P_x = Rs 6, P_y = Rs 4. Find the budget line equation and both intercepts.
Income = Rs 50, P_x = Rs 5, P_y = Rs 5. Is (6X, 2Y) affordable? Justify.

concepts.title: Consumer Equilibrium - Indifference Curve Approach
concepts.definition: A consumer is in equilibrium at the point where the budget line is tangent to the highest attainable indifference curve. At this point, MRS equals the price ratio.
concepts.key_idea: Equilibrium is where the slope of the indifference curve equals the slope of the budget line and income is fully spent.
question_patterns: find consumer equilibrium using indifference curve and budget line
verify that MRS equals price ratio at equilibrium
determine equilibrium combination of two goods
check tangency condition between budget line and indifference curve
compute MRS at a given combination and compare with price ratio

solution_steps.action: Compute MRS at the candidate combination
solution_steps.explain: MRS_xy = MU_x / MU_y at the given quantities.
The slope of the budget line is P_x / P_y.
Equilibrium holds if MRS = P_x/P_y and P_x*X + P_y*Y = M.

worked_examples.question: At combination (4X, 6Y), MU_x = 20, MU_y = 30. P_x = 4, P_y = 6, income = 52. Is this equilibrium?
worked_examples.solution: MRS = 20/30 = 0.667. Price ratio = 4/6 = 0.667. MRS = price ratio. Budget: 4*4 + 6*6 = 16+36 = 52 = M. Equilibrium holds.

worked_examples.question: At (3X, 5Y), MU_x = 30, MU_y = 20. P_x = 5, P_y = 4, income = 35. Is this equilibrium?
worked_examples.solution: MRS = 30/20 = 1.5. Price ratio = 5/4 = 1.25. MRS != price ratio. Not equilibrium.

exercises.question: At (5X, 4Y), MU_x = 24, MU_y = 18. P_x = 6, P_y = 4.5, income = 48. Check equilibrium.
Explain why the consumer is not in equilibrium if MRS > P_x/P_y.

compute_steps.action: substitute the given values into the formula

concepts.title: Demand and Market Demand
concepts.definition: Demand is the quantity of a commodity that a consumer is willing and able to buy at a given price in a given time period. Market demand is the sum of individual demands of all consumers.
concepts.formula: Market Demand = sum of individual demands Q_d = q1 + q2 + ... + qn
concepts.key_idea: Market demand is obtained by horizontal summation of individual demand curves.
question_patterns: compute market demand by summing individual demands
construct market demand schedule from individual schedules
find total quantity demanded at a given price
derive market demand curve from individual demand data
compute individual demand given market demand and others

solution_steps.action: List individual quantities demanded at each price
solution_steps.explain: Tabulate each consumer's demand at each price level.

solution_steps.action: Sum individual demands at each price
solution_steps.explain: Market demand at each price is the sum of all individual demands at that price.
Tabulate price against the corresponding market demand.

worked_examples.question: At price Rs 10, consumer A demands 20 units, B demands 30 units, C demands 50 units. Find market demand.
worked_examples.solution: Market demand = 20 + 30 + 50 = 100 units.

worked_examples.question: Individual demand schedules: A: (P=5, Q=40), (P=10, Q=30); B: (P=5, Q=20), (P=10, Q=15). Find market demand at each price.

exercises.question: At price Rs 8, demands of three consumers are 15, 25, 40. Find market demand.
Two consumers have demands 30 and 20 at price Rs 6. Market demand is 50. Verify.

concepts.title: Determinants of Demand and Demand Function
concepts.definition: Demand for a commodity depends on its own price, prices of related goods, income of the consumer, tastes and preferences, and other factors. The demand function expresses quantity demanded as a function of these factors.
concepts.formula: Q_d = f(P_x, P_y, P_z, Y, T, ...)
concepts.key_idea: Own price, related goods' prices, income, and tastes all influence the quantity demanded of a commodity.
question_patterns: identify factors affecting demand for a commodity
distinguish between movement along and shift of demand curve
explain effect of income change on demand
explain effect of substitute and complementary good price changes
write the demand function for a commodity

solution_steps.explain: Determine whether own price, related good price, income, or tastes changed.
A change in own price causes movement along the demand curve; changes in other factors shift the curve.

solution_steps.action: State the direction of change in demand
solution_steps.explain: Normal goods: income up -> demand up. Inferior goods: income up -> demand down. Substitute price up -> demand up. Complement price up -> demand down.

worked_examples.question: The price of tea rises. How does this affect demand for coffee (a substitute)?
worked_examples.solution: As tea becomes more expensive, consumers switch to coffee, so demand for coffee increases (demand curve shifts right).

worked_examples.question: Consumer income increases. How does demand for an inferior good change?
worked_examples.solution: For an inferior good, as income rises, consumers buy less of it, so demand decreases (demand curve shifts left).

exercises.question: The price of petrol rises. How does this affect demand for cars (a complement)?
Distinguish between a change in quantity demanded and a change in demand.

concepts.title: Demand Schedule and Demand Curve
concepts.definition: A demand schedule is a table showing quantity demanded at various prices. A demand curve is the graphical representation of the demand schedule, typically downward sloping due to the law of demand.
concepts.key_idea: The law of demand states that, other things equal, quantity demanded falls when price rises, giving a downward-sloping demand curve.
question_patterns: construct a demand schedule from a demand function
plot quantity demanded against price
compute quantity demanded at a given price from demand function
find price given quantity from demand function
verify inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded

solution_steps.explain: Use the given linear form Q_d = a - b*P.

solution_steps.action: Compute quantity demanded at each price
solution_steps.explain: Substitute each price value into the demand function.
Check that as price increases, quantity demanded decreases.

worked_examples.question: Demand function is Q_d = 100 - 5P. Find quantity demanded at P = 8 and P = 12.
worked_examples.answer: Q = 60 at P=8; Q = 40 at P=12

worked_examples.question: Demand function Q_d = 50 - 2P. Find the price at which demand is 30 units.

exercises.question: Demand function Q_d = 200 - 10P. Find quantity demanded at P = 5, 10, 15.
Demand function Q_d = 80 - 4P. Find the price at which demand is 20 units.

concepts.title: Price Elasticity of Demand
concepts.definition: Price elasticity of demand measures the percentage change in quantity demanded in response to a percentage change in price.
concepts.formula: Ed = (percentage change in quantity) / (percentage change in price) = (delta Q / Q) / (delta P / P)
concepts.key_idea: Elasticity is negative for normal goods due to the inverse price-quantity relationship; its magnitude determines elasticity classification.
question_patterns: compute price elasticity of demand using percentage method
classify demand as elastic, inelastic, or unitary
find percentage change in quantity given elasticity and price change
compute elasticity from demand function
compare elasticity at different points on a demand curve

solution_steps.explain: Calculate percentage change in quantity and percentage change in price.
Ed = (percentage change in quantity) / (percentage change in price).
|Ed| > 1 elastic, |Ed| = 1 unitary, |Ed| < 1 inelastic, |Ed| = 0 perfectly inelastic, |Ed| = infinity perfectly elastic.

worked_examples.question: Price rises from Rs 10 to Rs 12, quantity demanded falls from 50 to 40. Find Ed.
Price falls from Rs 20 to Rs 18, demand rises from 100 to 150. Find Ed.

exercises.question: Price rises from Rs 5 to Rs 6, demand falls from 80 to 70. Find Ed and classify.
Ed = -2. Price falls by 5%. Find the percentage change in quantity demanded.

concepts.title: Measurement of Elasticity - Total Outlay and Geometric Methods
concepts.definition: The total outlay method measures elasticity by observing how total expenditure changes with price. The geometric method measures elasticity at a point on a linear demand curve using segment ratios.
concepts.formula: Geometric: Ed = (lower segment) / (upper segment); Total outlay: compare change in total expenditure
concepts.key_idea: If price and total outlay move in opposite directions, demand is elastic; same direction, inelastic; no change in outlay, unitary.
question_patterns: measure elasticity using total outlay method
compute elasticity at a point on linear demand curve using geometric method
classify elasticity from total expenditure data
find elasticity using lower and upper segments of demand curve
compare total outlay and percentage methods of elasticity

solution_steps.action: Compute total outlay at each price
solution_steps.explain: Total outlay = Price * Quantity demanded.
If outlay moves opposite to price, demand is elastic; same direction, inelastic; unchanged, unitary.
On a linear demand curve, Ed = (lower segment from point) / (upper segment from point).

worked_examples.question: At P=10, Q=20; at P=12, Q=15. Use total outlay method to classify elasticity.
worked_examples.solution: Outlay1 = 10*20 = 200. Outlay2 = 12*15 = 180. Price rose, outlay fell (opposite direction). Demand is elastic.

worked_examples.question: On a linear demand curve, the point divides the curve into lower segment 4 and upper segment 6. Find Ed.
worked_examples.solution: Ed = lower / upper = 4/6 = 0.67.

exercises.question: At P=8, Q=50; at P=10, Q=40. Use total outlay method to classify elasticity.
A point on a linear demand curve divides it into lower segment 6 and upper segment 4. Find Ed.
